message.content: Painting the entire Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that depends on a lot of variables—weather, safety protocols, the type of paint, whether you’re doing a full overhaul or just touch‑ups, and how many crews you have working at once. In practice, the tower’s owners schedule a major repaint roughly every seven years, and the actual “painting” phase lasts only a few weeks (typically 10–14 days) of continuous work. However, because of safety constraints, the work is usually broken up into short shifts and spread out over a couple of months to keep the tower open to visitors and to allow for proper drying times between coats. So while the whole project might stretch over a few months, the core painting effort itself is usually around two weeks of active labor.
